answer: Topological Persistence Scoring. Each agent's score is the share of its neighbors that remain connected after random node removal, sampled from its real interaction graph. To wander across many clusters, an agent must maintain long-lived links in each; isolated clusters become an island with no score. Sybils that bridge cheaply leave a distinct cipher in the removal pattern. Cost: an attacker must sustain genuine bidirectional traffic across every forged region, paying bandwidth and latency per identity that grows with the number of clusters it fakes.
